newsitem.title: USA: NFL-HOLMGREN ON TOP OF FOOTBALL WORLD WITH PACKERS WIN.
newsitem.headline: NFL-HOLMGREN ON TOP OF FOOTBALL WORLD WITH PACKERS WIN.

text.p: The Pack is back on top of the football world and Green Bay is once again Titletown, USA after a wait of nearly three decades, courtesy of the Packers' 35-21 Super Bowl victory over the New England Patriots at the Louisiana Superdome on Sunday.
So Green Bay's Mike Holmgren has achieved everything he could possibly have hoped for when he took the job of Packers head coach five years ago, right? Well, not quite.

"Before I'm finished coaching, I would like to beat the Cowboys one time, that would be nice," Holmgren quipped on Monday at the traditional day-after news conference for the winning Super Bowl coach.
"I honestly didn't think about the Cowboys at all during the game," he joked.
His 0-7 record against Dallas notwithstanding, the easy-going, motorcycle-riding, big teddy bear of a man was looking pretty much like the cat that ate the canary Monday.
"Right now we're at the top of the world and I'm feeling very, very good about it," he beamed.

And why not. After all the talk of possibly being out-coached by New England's Bill Parcells and labouring in the shadow of legendary former Packers coach Vince Lombardi, Holmgren has stepped out into the sunlight of a bright new day.
"I think bringing the trophy back home is a wonderful thing," he said of the Super Bowl championship hardware that bears Lombardi's name.
"It's a wonderful thing for our fans... for all the people that have been there and filled that stadium (Green Bay's Lambeau Field) through thick and thin."

Five head coaches before Holmgren tried and failed miserably to live up to the Green Bay legacy of Lombardi, who won five NFL titles in the 1960s, including the first two Super Bowls before his retirement in 1967.
Holmgren has now permanently earned his place in the hearts of Green Bay's hysterically loyal fans.

And while he will have to drive down Lombardi Avenue to Lambeau Field later on Monday, the more than 60,000 fans expected to attend the sure-to-be wild victory rally will be cheering for Holmgren and HIS Green Bay Packers.
"We're going to go back to a full stadium now for our celebration," he said. "I'm very, very happy for those people."
The 48-year-old Holmgren may be a native of San Francisco. But as far as the people of Wisconsin are concerned, no matter what happens down the road, Mike Holmgren will always be a Green Bay Packer.
And, who knows, a couple more Super Bowl victories and some future Green Bay coach may have to cross the intersection of Lombardi Avenue and Holmgren Boulevard.
